skill.name: nestjs-oop-design-patterns
skill.description: Applies pragmatic OOP, SOLID, object-design rules, and design patterns to NestJS and TypeScript code. Use when writing or refactoring controllers, providers, use cases, entities, value objects, repositories, adapters, factories, strategies, handlers, or tests; when diagnosing god services, primitive obsession, inheritance misuse, duplicated conditionals, or leaky abstractions; and when selecting a pattern without over-engineering. Do not use for pure functional codebases or non-NestJS frontend work. When other skills also apply, reconcile ownership before mutation.
skill.summary: Improve NestJS object responsibilities, protect domain invariants, and select design patterns using concrete code evidence.
skill.author: amirtaherkhani

content.user_title: Refactor NestJS Code with Pragmatic Design Patterns
content.value_statement: Unclear responsibilities and unnecessary abstractions make NestJS code difficult to change and test. This skill guides evidence-based object design, pattern selection, and behavior-preserving refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Evaluate object responsibilities, encapsulation, collaborator contracts, and SOLID trade-offs using code evidence.
Distinguish entities, value objects, domain policies, application use cases, infrastructure adapters, and transport DTOs.
Select Strategy, Factory, Builder, Adapter, and other patterns based on real variation or failure modes.
Map cross-cutting concerns to Nest modules, providers, guards, pipes, interceptors, and exception filters.
Guide incremental refactoring with characterization tests, provider rewiring, and contract verification.
Explain reliability boundaries for in-process events, CQRS dispatch, transactional outbox, and sagas.
limitations: Targets NestJS and TypeScript object-oriented code, not pure functional codebases or unrelated frontend work.
Provides design guidance rather than a bundled executable refactoring engine.
Requires repository context, installed versions, callers, and tests to justify specific changes.
Does not make events durable or CQRS scalable without explicit infrastructure and verification.

use_cases.title: Review an overloaded service
use_cases.description: Identify unrelated responsibilities and propose a small refactor that preserves behavior and public contracts.

use_cases.title: Choose a provider integration pattern
use_cases.description: Compare direct integration, Adapter, and Strategy using vendor coupling, variation, and substitution requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan contract-focused verification
use_cases.description: Define tests for invariants, adapter substitution, Nest provider wiring, and transport behavior before refactoring.

prompt_templates.title: Understand one object
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [class] and its callers. Explain its role, responsibilities, and one concrete design concern without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand an existing controller or provider

prompt_templates.title: Select the smallest design
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare a direct solution, Strategy, and Factory for [observed variation]. Recommend one using repository evidence and explain its testing cost.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: choose a pattern for a real requirement

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a service safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [service] to separate [misplaced responsibility]. Preserve public behavior and user changes, add focused tests, and verify Nest provider wiring.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: implement an authorized responsibility change

prompt_templates.title: Review consistency and substitution
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [workflow] for adapter substitution, transaction boundaries, and event delivery guarantees. Compare direct coordination with outbox or saga designs and specify contract tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evaluate reliability across multiple boundaries

output_examples.input: A checkout service validates orders, calls a payment SDK, and maps database rows.
output: Role: The checkout use case coordinates order placement.
Evidence: Vendor payment details and persistence mapping change for different reasons.
Recommendation: Keep coordination in the use case and move vendor translation into an application-owned payment adapter.
Trade-off: The adapter adds a boundary and requires contract tests.
Verification: Preserve payment errors, order invariants, and provider wiring with focused tests.

output_examples.input: Should a service with one stable pricing rule use Strategy?
output: Evidence: Only one pricing algorithm exists, with no accepted requirement for another.
Recommendation: Keep the direct implementation rather than adding interchangeable policy classes.
Verification: Test pricing behavior and invariants through the public operation.

output_examples.input: Does an in-process event guarantee publication after a database commit?
output: Finding: In-process notification does not provide durable delivery across crashes or replicas.
Recommendation: Consider a transactional outbox when external consumers must reliably observe committed changes.
Trade-off: A relay requires retries, retention, ordering decisions, and idempotent consumers.

best_practices: Inspect callers, tests, module wiring, and repository conventions before selecting a pattern.
State the concrete problem, simpler alternative, and added cost before introducing an abstraction.
Preserve behavior with focused tests and verify contracts and provider wiring after refactoring.
anti_patterns: Adding interfaces, factories, repositories, or class hierarchies without real variation or a useful boundary.
Judging design only by line counts or applying fixed size limits as mandatory rules.
Assuming CQRS dispatch, in-process events, or pattern names provide durability or scalability.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets NestJS and TypeScript object-oriented backend code, including controllers, providers, domain objects, adapters, and tests.

faq.question: Does every class need an interface?
faq.answer: No. Add application-owned contracts for volatile effects, real variation, or useful testing boundaries, not every local class.

faq.question: Will it always recommend a design pattern?
faq.answer: No. It recommends the direct implementation when repository evidence does not justify additional abstraction.

faq.question: Are the related NestJS skills required?
faq.answer: No. They are optional coordination references when installed and relevant to overlapping decisions.

faq.question: Which tests should accompany a refactor?
faq.answer: Use focused behavior tests, adapter contract tests, and module wiring checks according to the changed boundary.

faq.question: Does a Nest event bus guarantee durable delivery?
faq.answer: No. Reliable external publication requires explicit persistence, delivery, recovery, and idempotency design, such as a transactional outbox.
